subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should native OpenAI cache-TTL pruning use the existing generic TTL clock, a retention-aware OpenAI policy, or a new provider-agnostic pruning mode before the linked fix can land?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but enabling the existing gate changes upgrade behavior for users whose OpenAI cache-TTL config was previously inert and may prune while OpenAI cache retention is still expected to matter.

options.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
options.body: Require the fix to align pruning timing with OpenAI cache-retention behavior and include native idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Accept existing TTL semantics
options.body: Maintain the current cache-TTL clock for OpenAI and explicitly document/test that existing OpenAI configs become active after upgrade.

options.title: Pursue provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Pause the provider-eligibility fix and implement a separate pruning mode that is not coupled to prompt-cache eligibility.

recommendation.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
recommendation.body: Require the fix to align pruning timing with OpenAI cache-retention behavior and include native idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced cache-TTL pruning and the prompt-caching docs, so he is the best history-backed owner for the product semantics decision.
